Lyndon B. Johnson was the President of the United States in 1965 [d1][d6][d7]. He was inaugurated on January 20, 1965, having won the 1964 presidential election with 61 percent of the popular vote [d6][d2]. During 1965, Johnson advanced his landmark Great Society legislative agenda, including signing the Voting Rights Act on August 6, 1965, and the Housing and Urban Development Act on August 10, 1965 [d5][d4][d2]. He also held a press conference on July 28, 1965, announcing an expansion of U.S. military involvement in Vietnam [d3].
